title: Linux OS Monitoring
summary: Inspect a Linux machine and its applications through osquery and six read-only MCP tools; investigate CPU, memory, filesystem usage, service health and recent history.

platform.product: Oracle AI Database Private Agent Factory

memory.description: Fresh tool evidence per question; recent measurements are retained by the monitoring service independently of Agent Memory.

capabilities: CPU and memory with measured assigned limits and explicit units.
osquery process and listener evidence, plus two application APIs and three background jobs.
Timestamped findings and actual coverage of up to 30 minutes of measurements.
Application roles, process IDs, health checks, work counters and human follow-up.
prerequisites: An x86_64 Linux host with Podman, enforceable cgroup CPU/memory/pids controls, slirp4netns and a private route from Factory.
The monitoring service deployed with documented resource caps and private source firewall allowlist.
Factory 26.7 and configured OpenAI Compatible model AIW26-PAF-HOL6004-BOO6096.
Administrator-approved HTTP outbound access and private destinations permitted in Factory, or a trusted private HTTPS endpoint.

tools.name: get_system_overview
tools.purpose: Linux OS identity, assigned resources, operations filesystem and history coverage.

tools.name: get_resource_usage
tools.purpose: One-second CPU, charged memory, assigned limits and process count.

tools.name: get_top_processes
tools.purpose: Bounded osquery process CPU and RSS samples, without command arguments.

tools.name: get_filesystem_usage
tools.purpose: Operations filesystem bytes, inodes and configured capacity.

tools.name: get_service_network_status
tools.purpose: Orders and inventory HTTP health, background job activity and osquery listeners.

tools.name: get_recent_history
tools.purpose: Actual ten-second samples, at most 30 minutes and 181 rows.

safetyControls: Six read-only tools; no SQL, shell, scenario-control or remediation tool.
Private source allowlist and firewall deny rule; no authentication or public listener is provisioned.
One CPU, 1536 MiB memory including swap, 128 pids, read-only root filesystem, no capabilities and bounded tmpfs.
Operator faults expire after 10–300 seconds; switching/resetting removes the previous fault.
Machine, filesystem and history coverage remain explicit; tool failures cannot establish health.
setup: Follow integrations/linux-os-monitoring/README.md to deploy the monitoring service. Infrastructure automation belongs in ~/work/infra/ansible.

Check the instance outbound URL policy: the private HTTP endpoint needs administrator-approved ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP_URLS=true and BLOCK_PRIVATE_OUTBOUND_URLS=false. Add Linux OS Monitoring as a Direct connection MCP source at http://HOST:8085/mcp and discover the six documented tools.
Import linux-os-monitoring.paf and select the new local source on the MCP server node; review the six allowed tools. Environment-local source IDs are not portable.
Select AIW26-PAF-HOL6004-BOO6096 on the Agent node. Configure that same OpenAI Compatible model name in every target instance; credentials/model definitions are not bundled.

Disable Agent Memory and sharing between chat threads; exported archives do not carry these switches. Read the sticky notes left to right, then expand Agent description for the walkthrough and sample questions.
Run the baseline prompt, then trigger one scenario with labctl as an operator, ask its matching question and reset. Review the draft before publishing.

sessions.title: Machine health, resource investigations and application activity

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Give me a health summary of this Linux machine: CPU, memory, disk and applications. State the observation time.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: CPU looks busy. Which processes explain it, and does recent history show sustained pressure?

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Is memory increasing? Compare actual available samples and identify the largest resident processes without claiming a leak.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Is the operations filesystem nearly full? How much space remains, and which filesystem did you measure?

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: The orders application is unavailable. Is its service listening, and are inventory and monitoring still reachable?

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Which applications and background jobs are running? Explain their roles, process IDs and recent activity.

expectedOutcomes: A severity, timestamped evidence for linux-ops-01, measured limits and human next step.
Faults are diagnosed from measured CPU, memory, disk and service evidence; the Agent changes nothing.
History reports actual time coverage, not an assumed 30-minute observation.

validation.environment: Private monitoring endpoint and Agent Factory
validation.status: Verified private connection and six conversations; unpublished draft
notes: 14 monitoring/lifecycle tests and 14 repository tests passed; all 29 archives passed decrypt-and-compare validation.

Private MCP discovery, five-application activity, four fault scenarios, automatic recovery and source restrictions passed. Unchanged deployment reapply reported zero changes. The eight-node Builder layout has no overlaps or clipping.

The approved HTTP setting is enabled on the configured instance and its private MCP source is connected. AIW26-PAF-HOL6004-BOO6096 answered all six questions in fresh rooms: baseline, application activity, CPU, memory, disk and service outage. Independent readings corroborated the answers; all retained explicit scope, limits, machine presentation and read-only follow-up.

The draft is unpublished, Agent Memory is disabled, and the portable native export has no environment-local source binding. Repeat import, binding, model and conversation checks on each final instance; see assets/validation.md.

catalog.question: What is putting this Linux machine under pressure, and which applications explain it?
